title: Free slots in library study rooms
prompt:
A library's study rooms open 09:00–18:00. All bookings are for the same day and are stored as start and end times. Some bookings overlap (the old system allowed it), and some start before opening or end after closing.

List every free slot of at least 30 minutes inside opening hours for every room in rooms. A slot ends where a booking starts, and starts where all earlier bookings have ended.

- Columns: room, free_from, free_until, free_minutes
- free_from and free_until are text 'HH24:MI'; free_minutes is an integer
- Order by room, then free_from
- A room with no bookings is free 09:00–18:00 (540 minutes)
- Only the part of a booking inside 09:00–18:00 matters; a booking ending at 09:00 blocks nothing
hints: Free time is the gap between merged busy intervals, plus the edges at opening and closing. Clip bookings to 09:00–18:00 first.
Add two zero-length sentinel rows per room, at 09:00 and at 18:00. Then a free slot runs from the furthest end seen so far to the next start.

Use max(e) OVER (PARTITION BY room ORDER BY s, e ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) as prev_end and keep rows where s - prev_end >= interval '30 minutes'. Format with to_char(date '2000-01-01' + t, 'HH24:MI').

exercise.starter:
-- Free slots between consecutive bookings
WITH b AS (
  SELECT room, starts_at,
         lag(ends_at) OVER (PARTITION BY room ORDER BY starts_at) AS prev_end
  FROM bookings
)
SELECT room,
       to_char(date '2000-01-01' + prev_end, 'HH24:MI') AS free_from,
       to_char(date '2000-01-01' + starts_at, 'HH24:MI') AS free_until,
       (extract(epoch FROM starts_at - prev_end) / 60)::int AS free_minutes
FROM b
WHERE starts_at - prev_end >= interval '30 minutes'
ORDER BY room, free_from;
exercise.solution:
WITH b AS (
  SELECT room,
         greatest(starts_at, time '09:00') AS s,
         least(ends_at, time '18:00') AS e
  FROM bookings
  WHERE ends_at > time '09:00' AND starts_at < time '18:00'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT room, time '09:00', time '09:00' FROM rooms
  UNION ALL
  SELECT room, time '18:00', time '18:00' FROM rooms
), w AS (
  SELECT room, s,
         max(e) OVER (
           PARTITION BY room ORDER BY s, e
           ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
         ) AS prev_end
  FROM b
)
SELECT room,
       to_char(date '2000-01-01' + prev_end, 'HH24:MI') AS free_from,
       to_char(date '2000-01-01' + s, 'HH24:MI') AS free_until,
       (extract(epoch FROM s - prev_end) / 60)::int AS free_minutes
FROM w
WHERE s - prev_end >= interval '30 minutes'
ORDER BY room, prev_end;

hiddenTests.name: 29 minutes is too short
hiddenTests.seed:
INSERT INTO rooms VALUES ('Carrel');
INSERT INTO bookings VALUES (1, 'Carrel', '09:29', '17:00'), (2, 'Carrel', '17:29', '18:00');

explanation: Free time is the complement of the union of bookings, so the query must look at the furthest end reached so far, not just the previous booking's end. Clipping bookings to opening hours and adding zero-length sentinels at 09:00 and 18:00 turns the edges of the day into ordinary gaps, and a room with no bookings gets one 09:00–18:00 slot for free. The running max of e over earlier rows, compared with each row's start, yields exactly the gaps between merged busy blocks. Traps: lag(ends_at) reports fake gaps inside a long booking that contains shorter ones, ignoring rooms with no bookings, and forgetting that a slot of exactly 30 minutes qualifies (>=) while 29 does not.
notes: time - time yields an interval, and date + time yields a timestamp, which is how to_char formats it since Postgres has no to_char(time). With real multi-day data you would use tsrange or tstzrange: range_agg merges the bookings and multirange subtraction (tsmultirange(opening) - range_agg(...)) returns free slots directly. An index on bookings(room, starts_at) supports the window sort per room.
followUps: Return only the single longest free slot per room, earliest first on ties.
Rewrite it with multiranges: subtract the merged bookings from the opening-hours range.
